title: Adobe Firefly for Video: Pricing, Features & Full Guide
summary: Learn how Firefly video, partner models and Premiere AI tools differ. Compare resolution-based credit costs and calculate a realistic video-generation budget.
body_markdown:
## Quick answer


**Adobe Firefly can generate new video from text or images, while Premiere offers AI tools for creating media inside an edit and extending existing clips.**


Choose the workflow and model first: clip length, resolution, credit cost and supported controls differ. A Firefly subscription does not make every video operation unlimited.


For an editor already working in Premiere, the strongest reason to consider Firefly is the connection to the timeline. For someone choosing a standalone generator, compare the output requirements and cost of a usable shot before choosing a subscription. This guide uses Adobe documentation checked on September 12, 2026; it is not a hands-on quality benchmark.


Magic Hour publishes this guide and is included where relevant. We compare current documented plan, credit, usage, and access terms from linked first-party sources. This is a pricing reference rather than a quality ranking; verify the final checkout and exact product route before purchase.


## What can Firefly do for video?


- **Generate a new shot:** turn a prompt or starting image into video in Firefly.
- **Guide the camera or composition:** use supported reference controls to steer a generated shot.
- **Work inside Premiere:** generate video and sound effects without leaving the timeline.
- **Extend an existing clip:** add material at an edge with Generative Extend, subject to media restrictions.
- **Use partner models:** choose supported third-party models inside Adobe's interface, with their own settings and costs.


The[Firefly application](https://www.adobe.com/products/firefly.html) is broader than the **Firefly Video Model** . Selecting a partner model does not turn that model into Adobe's own model or give it identical capabilities.


## How to make a video in Firefly


1. Open[Adobe Firefly](https://firefly.adobe.com/) and choose **Video → Generate video** .
2. Select the model, resolution and aspect ratio. Confirm the displayed duration and credit estimate.
3. Write a brief describing one shot. Add a first or last frame if your chosen workflow supports it.
4. Choose the available camera or reference controls that the shot actually needs.
5. Generate, review and download a suitable take. Assemble it with the rest of your footage, sound and titles.


Adobe's[camera-reference instructions](https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/work-with-audio-and-video/work-with-video/match-camera-motion-to-reference-video.html) describe a Firefly Video workflow with a five-second duration and 24 fps. A motion-reference upload must be 5–10 seconds and under 200 MB; only its first five seconds guide the generation. A reference guides an output—it does not guarantee an exact copy.


An original starting brief might be: **A small desk lamp illuminates a notebook beside a window at dusk. Slow sideways camera move, warm light, no people, one continuous shot.** Evaluate the resulting shot against the intended edit instead of treating a detailed prompt as a guarantee.


For a product whose appearance must stay accurate, prepare an approved source image first. Our[reference-image workflow](https://magichour.ai/blog/how-to-use-reference-images-in-image-to-video) explains what to check before animating it.


## Composition, transparency and audio: check the exact workflow


Firefly's[composition reference](https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/work-with-audio-and-video/work-with-video/use-video-as-composition-reference.html) uses a source video's layout to guide new footage. Adobe notes that this control is unavailable when an image keyframe is added in the documented workflow. Do not plan around combining controls that the interface makes mutually exclusive.


For compositing, Adobe also documents[transparent-background video generation](https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/work-with-audio-and-video/work-with-video/generate-videos-with-transparent-backgrounds.html) . Supported settings narrow when transparency is enabled, and first or last reference frames must be transparent PNGs. Check the downloaded result in your actual compositor before producing a batch.


### Transparent video: plan the two-file handoff


In the[documented Firefly workflow](https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/work-with-audio-and-video/work-with-video/generate-videos-with-transparent-backgrounds.html) , select Firefly Video, then enable Advanced settings → Transparent background. Adobe lists five seconds and 24 fps as the defaults, with unsupported controls hidden. Use the white or black preview to inspect subject edges as well as the transparent preview.


Download produces a ZIP containing a foreground video and a separate alpha video. Bring both assets into an editor or compositor that can use the alpha as a matte; do not assume the download is a single ready-to-place transparent movie. Verify the paired files in the actual delivery application before generating a batch.


Audio generation is another model and workflow decision. Firefly offers sound-effect tools, and some partner video models offer their own audio capabilities. Do not assume every generated video contains dialogue, music or synchronized sound. Use our[video-with-audio comparison](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-video-generators-with-native-audio) when sound is part of the shot brief, or compare[sound-effect generators](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-sound-effect-generators) when you need a separate audio asset.


## What changed in Premiere?


Adobe's September 2026[Generative Media Tool](https://helpx.adobe.com/premiere/desktop/edit-projects/edit-with-generative-ai/generative-media-tool-overview.html) lets you select a timeline range, describe the media, choose a supported model and add the generated result as an editable clip. It supports video and sound effects, including optional reference frames from the sequence.


That is distinct from **Generative Extend** , which works at an existing clip's edge. Adobe's[current Extend documentation](https://helpx.adobe.com/premiere/desktop/edit-projects/edit-with-generative-ai/generative-extend-overview.html) says it cannot create or extend spoken dialogue and does not accept clips containing music. It also documents output restrictions: extensions are SDR and 8-bit, and source footage above 30 fps receives a 30 fps extension. Check compatibility before promising a seamless professional handoff.


The[Extend overview](https://helpx.adobe.com/premiere/desktop/edit-projects/edit-with-generative-ai/generative-extend-overview.html) also limits a clip to extension at its beginning or its end, not both. The original footage remains in its native format; the added material is the part generated as SDR, 8-bit and, for source footage above 30 fps, 30 fps. Only mono or stereo audio is supported, and existing dialogue is muted during the extension. If the shot must return to another editor, include the generated media saved in the project's Captured and Generated scratch-disk location, not just the original source file.


For a missing establishing shot, generate new media. For a little more room around an existing cut, assess Extend. For a missing spoken sentence, record or generate the required narration in an appropriate workflow instead.


## Firefly video pricing: calculate the job, not just the plan


Adobe's[US individual plan comparison](https://www.adobe.com/products/firefly/plans.html) lists Standard at $9.99/month and Pro at $19.99/month. Pro Plus and Premium have regular monthly prices of $49.99 and $199.99, with limited-time offers shown separately. Check your region, billing commitment, renewal price and offer terms at checkout.


The important video question is what your selected operation costs. Adobe's[generative credit FAQ](https://helpx.adobe.com/creative-cloud/apps/generative-ai/generative-credits-faq.html) lists these Firefly Generate Video rates at 24 fps:

**Worked example:** six five-second shots, with three attempts per shot, require 18 generations. At the listed 1080p rate, that is **9,000 credits** . At 720p it is **4,500 credits** . This is a planning scenario, not a measured acceptance rate; it excludes other operations and assumes no applicable unlimited-generation offer.


This is why “up to X videos” on a plan page is not enough to budget a project. Specify the model, resolution, duration, attempts and any extra audio or editing operations. If your account has an unlimited offer, confirm which models and operations it covers and when it ends. Partner-model charges are separate from the Firefly rate table.


Budget **Generative Extend** separately from Generate Video. Adobe's[current credit rate card](https://helpx.adobe.com/creative-cloud/apps/generative-ai/generative-credits-faq.html) lists 1080p at 30 fps for Extend at 125 credits per second and 4K at 30 fps at 175. An illustrative two-second 1080p/30 fps extension therefore uses 250 credits before retries or any applicable offer. The five-second Generate Video calculation above is a different operation and frame-rate setting; choose the row for the actual task.


## Can you use Firefly for commercial work?


Adobe describes its own Firefly models as designed for commercial use and explains model training and usage in the[Firefly FAQ](https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/get-started/learn-the-basics/adobe-firefly-faq.html) . That is not a blanket clearance of every input, output or partner model. Review the applicable terms and your rights to uploaded material for the actual project.


For client delivery, keep a record of the model, source assets and selected outputs. Review product details, people, text and any implied claims before approval. Preserve provenance information where your publishing workflow supports it.


## When should you choose another video tool?


Start with your constraint: a specific reference workflow, native audio, output format, budget or API requirement. Then compare the same shot brief rather than vendor highlight reels.


For options outside Adobe, see our[Firefly alternatives guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/adobe-firefly-alternative) and[image-to-video comparison](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-image-to-video-generators) . To try a browser-based Magic Hour workflow with an approved source image, open[image-to-video](https://magichour.ai/products/image-to-video) and check the model and estimated credits before generating.


Cloud shadows move slowly across the scene while foreground plants respond to a light breeze. The camera makes one gentle push forward. Preserve the original composition, subjects, and visual style. One continuous shot.


[Try in Image-to-Video](https://magichour.ai/create/image-to-video?prompt=Cloud%2520shadows%2520move%2520slowly%2520across%2520the%2520scene%2520while%2520foreground%2520plants%2520respond%2520to%2520a%2520light%2520breeze.%2520The%2520camera%2520makes%2520one%2520gentle%2520push%2520forward.%2520Preserve%2520the%2520original%2520composition%252C%2520subjects%252C%2520and%2520visual%2520style.%2520One%2520continuous%2520shot.)

## Frequently asked questions

Adobe offers limited free or complimentary access, but the allowance and paid features depend on the account and current offer. Check the balance and operation cost in Firefly before treating it as a free production workflow.


###


Do not assume it does. Check the apps included in your plan and whether your existing Premiere subscription has the access you need. Generative credits and an application license are separate things to verify.


###


Yes, Adobe supports partner models in relevant Firefly and Premiere workflows. For example, its[Runway video-editor guide](https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/firefly-video-editor/generate-videos/generate-videos-using-runway-video-models.html) documents model-specific settings. Availability inside Adobe does not establish feature parity with the provider's own application.
